title: What Return Should Investors Reasonably Expect?
summary: Explainer on realistic investment returns: why one percent a day and sustained outsized returns are implausible, and why recent market returns may not repeat.

assertions.quote: a one percent daily return can turn a 100 investment into twelve hundred and forty dollars after one year
very few people are able to achieve anything above 20 regularly over a 10 to 30 year period

verdicts.note: Persistence studies find almost no managers or individuals sustain large alpha.

assertions.quote: it's good to kind of gauge your expectation at the eight percent to 12 range as a general rule of thumb
over a 15-year period 86.9 of large cap managers 81.4 percent of mid cap managers and 81.5 percent of small cap managers fail to outperform
the people boasting about high returns tend to have short track records that are no longer than just a few years

verdicts.note: Short-window returns are dominated by variance and regime; persistence is rare.

assertions.quote: trading call options and taking on leverage are unlikely to bode well should we encounter a longer downturn

verdicts.note: Leveraged strategies suffer in drawdowns, though some hedged option strategies hold up.

assertions.quote: these factors in all likelihood are not going to be sticking around forever
